rounds.text: Redington Ltd is fundamentally under-appreciated because its intrinsic valuation offers a substantial margin of safety of 40.8%, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 679 per share against a market price of Rs 402 [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's market price requires only 8.8% earnings growth, whereas the business is delivering vastly superior growth, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month sales jump of 23% and profit growth of 42% [E17, E21, E47]. Operational efficiency strongly supports this value creation, as the company commands a stellar return on capital employed of 15.8% to 18.4% and an ROE of 16.9%, crushing sector benchmarks where sector median ROCE sits at just 7.1% [E10, E12, E13, E71]. Momentum and institutional backing reinforce the fundamental strength, highlighted by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, a rules-based screen score of 92 out of 100, and foreign institutional holdings increasing to 61.96% [E42, E51, E60]. Conceded: operating cash flow is only 32% of operating profit at Rs 231 Cr for Mar 2026, pointing to a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.18x that requires careful monitoring of receivables and accruals [E34, E35, E37].

Redington's valuation is stretched relative to its peers, trading at a P/E of 20.37x and an EV/EBITDA of 12.57x, both of which exceed sector benchmarks [E6, E11]. This premium is further evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 3.09x against a sector benchmark of 1.42x [E2, E7]. Despite reported profit growth, the quality of these earnings is poor as cash conversion stands at a mere 0.18x, a level that requires scrutiny of receivables and accruals [E34]. Operating cash flow represents only 32% of operating profit, while borrowings have increased to Rs 2,842 Cr alongside inconsistent 2% operating margins [E37, E40, E30, E32]. Institutional sentiment is turning cautious, as seen in the negative money flow and the decline in domestic institutional holdings to 16.37% [E44, E43, E65]. Conceded: [E17, E51]. The company has achieved strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 23% and maintains a high relative-strength rating of 100. However, with the stock sitting 95% of the way up its 52-week range and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.2%, the current price-led momentum appears ahead of fundamentals [E48, E53, E56].

The bear's valuation concerns ignore the fact that the company trades at a conservative P/E of 17.4 [E1] and easily justifies its metrics through superior efficiency, boasting an ROCE of 15.8% against a sector benchmark of 6.61% [E10] and an ROE of 14.67% against a sector benchmark of 5.08% [E9]. Conceded: [E6, E11]. The criticism of cash conversion overlooks that operating cash flow reached Rs 231 Cr alongside free cash flow of Rs 125 Cr [E35, E36], backed by a robust balance sheet with a modest debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x [E38]. While domestic holdings shifted slightly [E43], foreign institutions have actually increased their stake to 61.96% compared to 56.26% previously [E42]. Conceded: [E44, E65]. Furthermore, the strong momentum and price position [E48, E53, E56] are fully underpinned by exceptional fundamentals, including trailing twelve-month sales growth of 23% [E17], a 42% surge in TTM profit growth [E21], and a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 679 per share providing a substantial margin of safety of 40.8% [E45, E46].

Conceded: [E1, E35, E36, E38, E42]. The bull’s reliance on a 17.4 P/E ignores that key ratios peg the P/E at 20.37x above its sector benchmark [E6], alongside an elevated EV/EBITDA of 12.57x exceeding sector norms [E11]. While operating cash flow reached Rs 231 Cr [E35], profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection with a weak cash conversion ratio of just 0.18x, where operating cash flow accounts for a meager 32% of operating profit [E34, E37]. This disparity points to potential issues with receivables and accruals [E34]. Furthermore, the claim that fundamentals fully underpin current momentum [E48, E53, E56] overlooks the reality that price growth has outpaced profit growth over five years and recently, showing that expectations are running ahead of delivery [E56, E57]. Finally, the heavy reliance on price strength is belied by negative institutional money flow and domestic institutional reduction [E43, E44, E65], compounded by a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.2% [E53] and an extreme 42.7% annualised volatility [E54].

Conceded: [E34, E37, E53]. Despite concerns over cash conversion matching operating profits for March 2026 [E34, E37], the company nonetheless generated positive operating cash flow of Rs 231 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 125 Cr [E35, E36], while maintaining a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x [E38]. The bear’s critique of valuation [E6, E11] ignores that the fundamental P/E sits at a more modest 17.4x [E1], and that foreign institutions have actually *increased* their holding to 61.96% up from 56.26% [E42], showing strong backing despite domestic reduction [E43]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 679 per share against the market price of Rs 402, delivering a robust margin of safety of 40.8% [E45, E46]. A reverse DCF proves that the current price only bakes in an 8.8% growth rate, far below the 16.0% base-case assumption and well under the company's historical 5-year sales and profit growth rates of 16% [E15, E19, E47]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the stock a strong 92 out of 100 on the back of explosive recent performance, including a 42% surge in TTM profit growth and 35% YoY sales growth [E21, E60, E61, E63].

Conceded: [E42]. The bull claims a modest fundamental P/E of 17.4x [E1], but ignores that key ratio providers peg the P/E at 20.37x against an 18.85x sector benchmark and place EV/EBITDA at 12.57x against a 10.61x benchmark [E6, E11]. The reliance on DCF intrinsic value and reverse assumptions [E45, E47] glosses over severe cash realization risks where operating cash flow sits at just 32% of operating profit, yielding a weak cash conversion of 0.18x for March 2026 that warns of profits far ahead of actual cash [E34, E37]. Furthermore, while FII holdings rose [E42], domestic institutions trimmed their stake [E43], net institutional money flow is negative [E44], and the screen flags active institutional outflow [E65]. The bull's highlighted price performance actually confirms extreme extension, with the stock sitting 95% up its 52-week range [E48], trading -2.7% from its high [E49], and showing clear price-led divergence where price growth exceeds profit growth and expectations outpace delivery [E56, E57]. Finally, this momentum unfolds against a historical record of an 80.2% peak-to-trough drawdown [E53] and an inconsistent operating margin trend [E32, E33], leaving the price vulnerable despite recent profit spikes [E21, E63].
